findings: Linux main calls original::run_with_retention(retain); its Rust #[path] is a compile-time module location, not a runtime source lookup.

Native retain destructures explicit output/source_path/received_path. Node, catalog, plan, providers, journals and caches all derive from the absolute operation output. funding::open_node forwards that explicit path to Node::open_with_permanent_account_growth_v2.

The funding, grouped request and recovery helper source files have no current_dir/current_exe/CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/environment path lookup or fixed old host/repository path. groups_v3 constructs request metadata; recovery uses supplied owner objects and output.
Shared frozen-B CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR occurs only in include_str! for BOOTSTRAP. The embedded bytes are hashed and compared with the independently pinned sealed bootstrap member before execution.

Shared read_pinned requires every input path to be absolute. The child executable is spec.python.path, with -I -S -B -X private pycache_prefix and an environment cleared to LANG/LC_ALL/TMPDIR; model/environment material paths and Python identity come from the independently hashed source input.

No reviewed entry/callback code requires the ELF to remain beside the original Cargo source tree. Copying the already accepted normal release ELF to a new create-only locator can preserve artifact identity, provided actual source/ELF readback and the new complete runtime/model operations pass.

This narrow source review does not prove arbitrary binary/system portability, unchanged dynamic loader/provider behavior, or new model execution. The original full source guard, full Python runtime guard, exact resource limits and new operation input/audit checks remain required.
